chunks: 1836 - Abu Ja‘far عليه السلام said to Jabir:

"O Jabir, whoever reaches the month of Ramadan, then fasts its days, stands for a portion of its night, guards his chastity and his tongue, lowers his gaze, and restrains his harm, will come out from sins like the day his mother gave birth to him."
Jabir said: "I said to him, 'May I be your ransom, how beautiful this hadith is!'" He said: "How severe this condition is."

key_terms.أَذَاهُ: his harm, meaning refraining from hurting others
key_terms.الذُّنُوبِ: sins, from which the fasting person is purified if the conditions are fulfilled
key_terms.بَصَرَهُ: his sight, meaning lowering the gaze from what is forbidden
key_terms.شَهْرُ رَمَضَانَ: the month of Ramadan, the sacred time of fasting and intensified worship
key_terms.فَرْجَهُ: his private chastity, meaning protection from unlawful sexual conduct
key_terms.فَصَامَ: he fasted, meaning he observed the obligatory sawm of the day
key_terms.لِسَانَهُ: his tongue, meaning restraint from sinful or harmful speech
key_terms.وِرْدًا: a regular portion of worship performed at night

ai.seo_question: What conditions in Ramadan lead to forgiveness of sins like a newborn child?
ai.summary: This hadith teaches that the full spiritual benefit of Ramadan comes through both fasting and moral discipline. It links sawm, night worship, chastity, control of speech, lowering the gaze, and refraining from harming others with complete forgiveness of sins. The Imam عليه السلام emphasizes that this reward is immense, but its conditions are demanding.
